blocks.text: Kisi system ka heat content ya enthalpy (H) do hisson se mil kar banta hai:

items: Woh hissa jo free (azad) hai aur doosri types ki energy mein badla ja sakta hai; ise Gibbs free energy, G, kehte hain.
Woh hissa jo system ko fixed temperature par maintain (qaim) rakhne ke liye zaroori hai; yeh kisi aur shakal mein nahi badla ja sakta (T × S).

blocks.text: Is equation se pata chalta hai ke system ki saari enthalpy sirf tab kaam aa sakti hai jab system zero kelvin par ho (kyun ke tab TS = 0).
Do alag alag states ki enthalpies ke farq ke liye yeh equation likhte hain:
Agar process constant (ek jaise) temperature par ho to:

blocks.latex: \Delta H = \Delta G + T\Delta S\quad (\text{at constant } T)

blocks.text: Free energy change (ΔG) ke sign se pata chalta hai ke process spontaneous hai ya nahi:

items: Agar ΔG < 0 (manfi) ho to process spontaneously (khud ba khud) ho sakta hai.
Agar ΔG > 0 (musbat) ho to process khud ba khud nahi ho sakta; balke us ka ulta process ho sakta hai.
Agar ΔG = 0 ho to na process khud hota hai na us ka ulta; system equilibrium (tawazun) mein hai.

blocks.prompt: Ek reaction ka ΔH positive aur ΔS negative hai. Kya yeh spontaneous hoga? Aur kin conditions mein reaction hamesha spontaneous hota hai?
blocks.explanation: Kabhi nahi: ΔG = ΔH – TΔS mein dono hisse har temperature par ΔG ko positive banate hain. Reaction hamesha spontaneous hota hai jab ΔH negative aur ΔS positive ho, kyun ke tab ΔG har temperature par negative hai.

items: H = G + TS: G enthalpy ka free hissa, TS temperature se bandha hissa; constant T par ΔG = ΔH – TΔS.
ΔG negative: spontaneous; positive: nahi (ulta ho sakta hai); zero: equilibrium.
